Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’m starting with the workspace contract and the required wake-visual inspection skill. That skill will determine which rollout keyframes I inspect before touching the target policy; I’ll keep all work inside this Phase 2 workspace.

The inherited evidence is unusually consistent: turn-rate damping improved upstream progress up to gain 0.70, but every sampled controller still loops upward and leaves the domain. I’m now comparing the best finite rollout against the stronger-gain failure, including the shared initial wake and released keyframes, before I choose the single continuation.

The visual comparison closes the previous search direction: gain 0.70 is still best; 0.80 and 1.05 both reduce posterior peak angle slightly but preserve the same upper-loop exit and regress navigation, while the more sensitive 0.25 scale is markedly worse. I’m recording that negative boundary first, then I’ll test one isolated posterior-servo change that leaves the proven anterior propulsion and 0.70/0.35 steering anchor intact.

The single candidate is now in place: it keeps the best 0.70/0.35 turn-rate anchor and tightens only body-frame bearing sensitivity from 25° to 20°, without increasing the 10° steering ceiling. The durable guidance now records the failed 0.80/1.05 gain and 0.25-scale bracket, so later workers won’t keep searching that exhausted axis. I’m moving into the mandated static contract checks now; no CFD will be run.
